prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable solution makes staple crops drought-proof, so the Main KPI of 1,000,000,000 people growing drought-proof crops is far from met. The best deployed answers are drought-tolerant, not drought-proof. HB4 wheat, approved in Argentina, gave a 13 percent field yield advantage under reproductive-stage water deficit in INTA's April 2026 Field Crops Research study and had about 100,000 ha planted cumulatively by 2024 (https://repositorio.inta.gob.ar/handle/20.500.12123/25002). DTMA drought-tolerant maize out-yields checks in managed trials, but in Malawi's 2011/12 early-season drought it did no better than other improved maize (https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s12571-015-0511-4), and modelled gains are 3 to 20 percent. Cereal losses in drought years still average 13.7 percent globally, and the UNCCD frames even 25 to 30 percent drought yield gains as tolerance, not immunity (https://www.unccd.int/resources/unccd-library/new-hostile-climate-drought-tolerant-crops-systems-needed-unprecedented). Europe PMC returns only 6 records for the phrase drought-proof crop, none reporting such a crop. Honest limit: drought tolerance in maize, wheat and sorghum is a mature field with released varieties, so tasks that re-breed or re-test HB4 or DTMA-type tolerance are known answers; the open work is crops that hold yield under severe, early or multi-season drought, and each task needs its own basis.
